tools.name: Cooking chopsticks or tongs
tools.note: For turning the meat and stirring.

steps.title: Mix the sauce first
steps.text: Combine the soy sauce, sugar, sake, and water in a small bowl and stir until the sugar dissolves. If you're using ginger, add it now.
steps.hint: If you start measuring after the heat is on, the pork overcooks while you do it. Making the sauce first is the single most effective move in this recipe.

steps.title: Slice the onion thinly
steps.text: Peel it, halve it lengthwise, and slice with the grain into pieces about 5 mm thick. This is the only time you need the cutting board, so wash it and the knife now. The pork needs no cutting.

steps.title: Spread the pork out and don't touch it
steps.text: Heat the oil over medium-high. Spread the pork so the pieces overlap as little as possible, then leave it alone for 1½ to 2 minutes. Flip only once the underside is well browned. That browning is the heart of the flavor.
steps.hint: If the pork is fatty, skip the oil. Stirring too early draws out moisture and you end up steaming the meat instead of searing it.

steps.title: Add the onion and let it soften
steps.text: Push the meat to one side and add the onion to the empty half. Cook for about 2 minutes, until translucent with lightly colored edges.

steps.title: Pour in the sauce and reduce
steps.text: Add the sauce from step 1. Keep it at a lively bubble, shaking the pan, for 1 to 2 minutes. When the sauce has thickened, clings to the meat, and turns glossy, kill the heat. If you're using butter, add it off the heat and let the residual warmth melt it.
steps.hint: Over-reduce and it suddenly turns salty. Stop while a little sauce still pools at the bottom of the pan.

steps.title: Serve over hot rice
steps.text: Heat the packed rice as directed, tip it into a bowl, and pile on the pork and onion. Scrape every last bit of sauce from the pan over the top.

troubleshooting.problem: The pork is tough or dry
troubleshooting.solution: It was overcooked. Thin-sliced pork is nearly done the moment it's browned. About 30 seconds after flipping is plenty, and the sauce finishes the rest.

troubleshooting.problem: The meat weeps water and won't brown
troubleshooting.solution: The pan wasn't hot enough, or the meat was piled up. Wait until the oil shimmers with a wisp of smoke, then spread the pieces flat. 150 g is the most one pan can sear at once.
The sauce wasn't reduced enough. Stopped while still watery, it soaks into the rice and turns thin. Boil it down until it's glossy and slightly thick.
Reduced too far. Add 1 tablespoon of water and bring it back to a brief simmer. Next time use 3 tablespoons of water for more margin.
It needed more heat. Cook until translucent, then give it one more minute in the sauce and the sharpness turns to sweetness.
Chopped scallions, shichimi pepper, an egg yolk, or mayonnaise. Pick exactly one. Stacking several muddies the flavor.
